newsitem.title: UK: NSEA Brent weaker on physical, paper markets.
newsitem.headline: NSEA Brent weaker on physical, paper markets.

text.p: Benchmark Brent crude dipped on physical and paper markets on Friday and some traders said they see wet North Sea differentials softer next week from ample avails.
A June 16-18 loader of Brent changed hands at 49 cents discount to July Brent, one cent lower than what a June 12-14 cargo fetched a day earlier, which was four cents below Tuesday's lowest level.
All four Brent cargoes turning wet on Friday were kept ahead of the five o'clock deadline, two by Stasco, and one each by BP and Phibro, traders said.
Stasco kept the June 21-23 and June 22-24 loaders, BP kept the June 23-25 cargo and Phibro kept a June 23-25, a deferral from June 18-20, the traders added.
Other North Sea were also slightly lower, with a Forties cargo loading June 26-28 traded at Dated Brent +17 cents, one cent off a deal for June 29-July 1 cargo traded a day earlier.
Traders said Forties was facing a bit of pressure with some June cargos still unsold, while Norwegian grades were also assessed a little softer.
"There seem to be a lot of June avails in Oseberg, Stafjord, Eko and Gullfaks," one trader said.
"All the Norwegian grades are talked lower by 10 to 15 cents but this is not backed up by deals," he added.
He said Ekofisk was assessed at about Dated Brent +10 cents, Oseberg at about Dated evens to Dated +10 cents and Statfjord at a 15 cents premium to Dated Brent.

There was unconfirmed talk of a late June Ekofisk fetching a few cents above Dated Brent and of a second dacade Oseberg and a third decade Flotta also moving on Friday. There were no further details available.
